Summarise person descriptives by variable

Source: R/stats_describe.R
summary.idiographic_descriptives.Rd

One row per variable, aggregating the per-person rows of a describe_persons() result: the number of persons, the mean and standard deviation of the person means, the average within-person standard deviation, and, when the result was computed with detail = "full", the number and share of persons whose linear trend is significant at alpha. With no trends present, the expected share is alpha.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'idiographic_descriptives'
summary(object, alpha = 0.05, ...)

# S3 method for class 'idiostats_descriptives'
summary(object, alpha = 0.05, ...)

Arguments

object

A describe_persons() result.

alpha

Significance level for counting linear trends.

...

Ignored.

Value

A data frame with one row per variable and columns variable, persons, mean_of_means, sd_of_means, mean_sd_within, significant_trends, and trend_share (the last two NA unless detail = "full").

Examples

d <- describe_persons(srl, id = "name", vars = c("efficacy", "effort"),
                      time = "day", detail = "full")
summary(d)
#>   variable persons mean_of_means sd_of_means mean_sd_within significant_trends
#> 1 efficacy      36      54.03965    15.90734       21.27906                  1
#> 2   effort      36      58.97604    14.54039       22.25366                  1
#>   trend_share
#> 1  0.02777778
#> 2  0.02777778
